summary: Adult-onset Stargardt disease patients (7, 29-69 years) underwent multimodal retinal imaging, including confocal and non-confocal Adaptive Optics Scanning Light Ophthalmoscopy (AOSLO), optical coherence tomography (OCT), fundus infrared (FIR), short wavelength-autofluorescence (FAF), and color fundus photography (CFP). Imaging modalities revealed alterations in retinal structure, including variable foveal structure and photoreceptor degeneration, which were correlated across imaging modalities. Dark cones, hypo-reflective gaps of non-waveguiding cones, were identified as a possible first sign of retinal disease progression in adult-onset Stargardt disease.
